edit.description: the root seam's claim narrows to what it proves, and a failing write under the resolved root is reported with that root
the awake dir's own mkdir, the measured throw site
the obstructed-write refusal, beside the not-a-directory seam's cases

summary: The root seam proves the state root stats as a directory, never that anything can be made under it, so a failing write past it exits 1 on a raw stack at every verb
acceptance: a write under the resolved state root that fails refuses at the point of detection, `EX_IOERR` naming the resolved root rather than the leaf an errno carried, so no verb reaches `main()`'s catch over an unusable root and the seam above states only the usability it actually proves
tests: flume wake exits EX_IOERR naming the resolved state root when the awake directory cannot be made
notes: Off note THE-OBSTRUCTED-STATE-ROOT-REFUSES-AT-ONE-SEAM, residual 1, measured decidably here: a plain file at `<flumeDir>/awake` makes `mkdirSync(.., { recursive: true })` (`src/Baton.ts:63`) throw EEXIST on every host and for every uid, so the shape instrument (`tests/helpers/denial.ts`) reaches it with no mode. `src/cli.ts:408` claims the root proven usable; `statLoud` (`:428`) proves it is a directory. `main()`'s catch (`:1744`) is the exit 1. Seams `src/cli.ts` with three standing entries.
